prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t name one single “best” company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and insurance situation. I can, however, help you find top-rated, hurricane-rated roofers near you and give a checklist so you can pick the best one confidently.

If you want company name recommendations, tell me your Miami zip code (or neighborhood) and whether this is residential or commercial. I’ll look up highly rated local contractors and show how to verify they’re properly qualified.

Meanwhile, use these criteria to identify the best hurricane-rated roofing contractor:

Must-haves
- Proper Florida contractor license (check DBPR license lookup).
- General liability and workers’ comp insurance (ask for certificates).
- Experience with Miami‑Dade County NOA products and systems (must use NOA-approved shingles/tiles/metal and methods).
- Proven wind‑uplift rated installation (ask for the uplift rating and the details of the attachment method).
- Local references and recent photos of completed hurricane-rated jobs.
- Written, itemized estimate and contract (include scope, materials, colors, start/completion dates, payment schedule).
- Manufacturer’s warranty plus a contractor workmanship warranty (get both in writing).

Red flags
- Asks for large upfront cash payment (typical safe max initial deposit is 10–30%).
- No local references or poor/very few reviews.
- Pressure to sign immediately or to use questionable payment methods.
- No permits pulled or reluctance to pull permits.

Top questions to ask each contractor
1. Are you licensed in Florida? What is your license number? (Verify via DBPR.)
2. Do you use Miami‑Dade NOA-approved materials for hurricane zones? Can you show the NOA?
3. What wind uplift rating will the new system achieve? Can you provide specs?
4. Who will pull the permits and handle inspections? Is that included?
5. What warranties are provided (manufacturer + workmanship)? How are warranty claims handled?

How I can help next
- If you give me your zip code/neighborhood and whether it’s a house or commercial building, I’ll list 3–5 highly rated local contractors and include how to verify their licenses, NOAs and reviews.
- Or I can draft an email/template you can send to contractors to request the information above.

Which would you prefer?
